story_pergunta: Do you know how often AI engines cite your company?

slides.eyebrow: AI ON THE RISE · BUSINESSES IN CHATGPT
slides.headline: ChatGPT now has a storefront. Does your content get cited?
slides.sub: A profile helps. It doesn't make AI read or cite you.

slides.headline: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT, in beta
slides.body: Through Business Hub, companies can claim their business, update their information and see insights like mentions and website clicks. Eligible US ecommerce and online service businesses can also launch a Business Agent.

slides.label: people use ChatGPT each week, according to OpenAI
slides.sub: That is the audience OpenAI says businesses can now connect with.

slides.headline: What I see in companies: a profile is not a strategy
items: The profile gets claimed, but the site content is still hard for AI to parse.
Nobody knows if AI engines actually read, cite or send traffic to the site.
The dashboard gets checked once, and no one owns the result.

slides.headline: For one of Brazil's largest cosmetics companies, I rebuilt an annual report for AI
items: Server-rendered HTML in 3 languages, Schema.org/JSON-LD, llms.txt, 17 AI crawlers allowed by name.
In 15 days: 1,427 AI crawler reads from 8 engines, 553 searches from real questions.
60 people reached the site by clicking an AI citation, tracked by an in-house log collector.

slides.headline: Measure instead of assuming.
slides.body: A business profile is a visibility feature. It becomes a result when you know how AI actually reads you, what triggers real questions and which citations get clicked. Without that separation, you are guessing.

slides.eyebrow: WANT TO SEE HOW I DID IT?
slides.headline: Comment GEO.
slides.body: I'll send you the step-by-step of this case by DM. I take AI off the drawing board and put it into production, with measured results.

caption:
OpenAI announced Businesses in ChatGPT today. In beta, Business Hub lets companies claim their business, keep information current and see insights like mentions and website clicks. TechCrunch framed it as ChatGPT moving closer to Google as a discovery engine.

In practice, I see a gap that a profile alone doesn't close. Being cited still depends on content AI can parse, and on knowing how you actually appear.

That is the problem I worked on with one of Brazil's largest cosmetics companies. We rebuilt an annual report to be read and cited by ChatGPT, Claude and Perplexity: server-rendered HTML in 3 languages, Schema.org/JSON-LD, llms.txt and 17 AI crawlers allowed by name.

Then we measured it with an in-house log collector that separates crawling, real questions and citation clicks. In 15 days: 1,427 reads by AI crawlers from 8 engines, 553 searches triggered by a real person asking a question, and 60 people who reached the site by clicking an AI citation.

Measure instead of assuming.

Comment GEO and I'll DM you how I did it.

Sources: openai.com, techcrunch.com
